newsitem.title: USA: Volvo GM Heavy Truck closing Ohio plant employing 473.
newsitem.headline: Volvo GM Heavy Truck closing Ohio plant employing 473.

text.p: Volvo GM Heavy Truck Corp. said Thursday that it was shutting its manufacturing plant in Orrville, Ohio, which employs 473 people.
The company said that after the plant is shut in April some employees there will be offered employment with at other Volvo locations, but it offered no specifics.
Volvo GM, a truck-making joint venture of the two automakers, said operations at the Ohio plant, which produces 15 trucks a day, will be moved to its manufacturing complex in Dublin, Va.
It said the consolidation will result in more efficient operations and lower manufacturing costs.

"The decision was a difficult one because we have a loyal, skilful work force in Orrville," President Marc Gustafson said in a statement. "But the savings we will realise from this consolidation are important for our future."
The company said its other manufacturing plants in Ohio were not affected by the decision.
Volvo GM, which is based in Greensboro, N.C., said the Orrville plant will be sold after it is shut.

The company, which manufactures Volvo highway tractors and trucks and markets heavy-duty and mid-range diesel engines, transmissions, and rear suspensions, is 87 percent owned by Volvo Truck Corp. of Gothenburg, Sweden, and 13 percent by General Motors Corp.
